title: Microsoft Teams: private chat for organisers and presenters in webinars, structured meetings and town halls
summary: Hold: Microsoft Learn now describes the private chat for webinars and structured meetings on Teams Rooms on Android, contrary to the briefing's documentation gap. Those release notes also mark the chat as requiring Teams Rooms Pro, so the blanket statement that no licence specific to this chat is published needs narrowing.

claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: Chat for organizers and presenters in structured meetings and webinars. Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters can chat privately in a separate chat from attendees.

claims.claim: MC1188222 unifies town hall backroom chat behaviour under roadmap item 392328.
claims.quote: Additionally, we are unifying backroom chat behavior in town halls to ensure consistent functionality across all structured meetings. This message is associated with Roadmap ID 392328

claims.claim: Existing backroom chat behaviour varies with streaming chat and the organiser's Teams Premium licence.
claims.quote: Currently, backroom chat behavior varies depending on whether streaming chat is enabled for town halls and whether the organizer has a Teams Premium license.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Town hall backroom chat becomes on by default regardless of streaming chat availability or licence type.
claims.quote: Unified backroom chat policy for town halls: The default setting will be ON for all town halls, regardless of streaming chat availability or license type.

claims.claim: Existing town halls adopt the new policy when meeting options are updated.
claims.quote: Existing town halls will adopt the new policy once meeting options are updated.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Turning the policy off removes backroom chat from already scheduled, previously enabled town halls on a meeting options update.
claims.quote: If an admin explicitly turns the new backroom chat policy OFF, any already-scheduled town hall that previously had backroom chat ON will lose access once the meeting options are updated.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Town halls without Teams Premium where backroom chat was off gain it by default after rollout and an options update.
claims.quote: For non-TPre town halls where backroom chat was previously OFF, it will switch to ON by default after the rollout and a meeting options update.

claims.claim: MC1188222 was updated on 1 September 2026.
claims.quote: Updated September 1, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: Targeted Release is planned from mid-October 2026 to late October 2026.
claims.quote: Targeted Release: Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 (previously late September) and is expected to complete by late October 2026 (previously late August).

claims.claim: General Availability for Worldwide and GCC begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide and GCC): Rollout begins in late October 2026 (previously mid-September) and is expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously early November).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The notice says to disable backroom chat through a Teams admin center policy but supplies no policy name or navigation path.
claims.quote: If you want to disable backroom chat, adjust the policy in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The separate chat for webinars and structured meetings is introduced with this rollout.
claims.quote: We're introducing a private chat feature for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in structured meetings and webinars in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Learn calls the town hall private chat the event group chat.
claims.quote: In events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, the chat experience differs depending on the event role. Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters can chat with each other in the event group chat.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Town hall event group chat is available before, during and after the event, separately from attendee chat.
claims.quote: The event group chat is available before, during, and after an event, and is a separate experience from the chat with attendees.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the separate chat for webinars and structured meetings.
claims.quote: When a Teams Rooms on Android is an organizer, co-organizer or presenter in a webinar and structured meeting, you have access to a private chat for event management known as the Event Group.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The Manage chat for Teams events article does not yet describe the separate chat for webinars and structured meetings; the November 2026 Teams Rooms on Android release notes describe it as the Event Group chat.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/rooms-release-note.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The event-chat article explicitly excludes event group chat from the attendee-chat mailbox storage rule.
claims.quote: Meeting chat messages in events optimized for large audiences, excluding the event group chat, are stored only in an organizer's mailbox for up to 30 days.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: General Teams group-chat documentation places compliance copies in all participants' Exchange Online mailboxes.
claims.quote: Exchange Online stores Teams compliance records that the substrate captures, and eDiscovery can access these records. Messages in group chats are stored in the Exchange Online mailbox of all chat participants.

claims.claim: External presenter support for event group chat is covered by a separate roadmap item.
claims.quote: 573706: Microsoft Teams: External presenter support for event group chat. Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting, will support external presenters.

claims.claim: The feature described is person-to-person chat rather than an autonomous action capability.
claims.quote: Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters can chat privately in a separate chat from attendees.

claims.claim: The chat is included within existing Teams licensing rather than requiring a separately purchased chat entitlement.
claims.quote: The default setting will be ON for all town halls, regardless of streaming chat availability or license type.

claims.quote: All eligible Teams licenses include the foundational capabilities needed to create and run events, engage attendees, review attendance reports, and publish event recordings.

claims.where: controls[0]; Governance controls; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents no admin UI path or PowerShell parameter for disabling backroom event group chat.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams event group backroom private chat organizers presenters webinars admin policy PowerShell licensing; "backroom chat" "policy"; opened manage-event-chat, plan-events, Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; no backroom path or parameter.

claims.claim: Plan for Teams events lists No control for admins over large-audience event group chat, unlike the notice's policy statement.
claims.quote: | Event group chat (organizers, co-organizers, and presenters) | No control. | Can chat with presenters and co-organizers. Attendees don't use this chat during events.

claims.claim: The Meeting chat control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting engagement > Meeting chat.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy you want to edit. Go to the Meeting engagement section. Set Meeting chat to your chosen value

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled disables meeting chat.
claims.quote: To turn off meeting chat for users with this assigned policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference says setting MeetingChatEnabledType to Disabled also requires setting LobbyChat to disabled.
claims.quote: Due to a new feature rollout, in order to set the value of MeetingChatEnabledType to Disabled, you will need to also set the value of LobbyChat to disabled.

claims.claim: Meeting chat governs reading and sending messages in meetings and events up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Whether participants in your users' meetings and events with up to 1,000 attendees can read and send chat messages.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly state whether Meeting chat governs the new separate webinar and structured-meeting chat.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams private separate organizer presenter webinar chat backroom licensing price meter meeting chat policy PowerShell; "private chat" "webinars" "structured"; read manage-meeting-chat, manage-event-chat, plan-events and rooms-release-note; no explicit separate-chat policy mapping.

claims.claim: The town hall attendee-chat control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience chat experience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. Select the policy you want to edit or create a new one. In the Events optimized for a large audience chat experience dropdown list, select Optimized (the default value) or None.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None prevents organisers enabling attendee chat.
claims.quote: None | Organizers with this policy can't turn on chat for their attendees. To turn off chat for attendees in events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None

claims.claim: Meeting chat is a per-user and per-organiser policy.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't apply to channel meetings and is a per-user and per-organizer policy.

claims.claim: Meeting chat policy does not apply to channel meetings.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't apply to channel meetings

claims.claim: Manage chat for Teams events gives Optimized as the attendee-chat policy default.
claims.quote: In the Events optimized for a large audience chat experience dropdown list, select Optimized (the default value) or None.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the events policy as preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference lists None as the TownhallChatExperience parameter default.
claims.quote:
### -TownhallChatExperience
Possible values are: Optimized, None.
| Default value: | None |

claims.claim: TownhallChatExperience is a user-level setting for attendee Comment Stream chat rather than the separate event group chat.
claims.quote: User-level policy for tenant admin to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. This setting governs whether the user can enable the Comment Stream chat experience for an event optimized for a large audience.
